summary: Beverly's Hospital Point light has shown since 1871 from a brick tower on the old smallpox-hospital point; its rear range light has been in a church steeple since 1927.

lens.where: Lantern of the 1872 brick tower. The 1981 Massachusetts form says a Fresnel was replaced in 1976 and an acrylic optic installed in 1981; the Digital Archive and LighthouseFriends describe a third-and-a-half-order Fresnel in place (see notes_for_editor)

access.note: Coast Guard property behind a private road, fence and gate. The dwelling is closed; the Coast Guard opens the grounds and tower once a year during Beverly Homecoming. The rear light is in a church steeple and is not open to the public.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (owner; First Coast Guard District). Rear light: First Baptist Church (building), Coast Guard (optic)

corrections.why: The Digital Archive gives the original and current optic as third-and-a-half-order Fresnel, and LighthouseFriends says the same. The record's 'order 3' is not supported. The 1981 form's acrylic optic note is in dispute (see resolved_conflicts).

corrections.proposed: about 12.2 m (40 ft) per the 1981 form; the Digital Archive gives 45 ft from base to lantern centre
corrections.why: The form says the tower is 40 feet high and the Digital Archive gives 45 feet to the lantern centre; the record's 13.5 m matches neither exactly.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1981 Massachusetts form says a Fresnel lens was replaced in 1976 and an acrylic optic installed in 1981. The Digital Archive (current optic: third-and-a-half-order Fresnel) and LighthouseFriends (one of about five Massachusetts Fresnels still active in 2010) describe a Fresnel in place. Both can be true only if the 1981 optic was later removed or the form is wrong. Not resolved.

The 1981 form gives the tower as 40 feet high (14'7" diameter). LighthouseFriends gives 45 feet (a forty-five-foot-tall tower) and the Digital Archive gives 45 feet from base of structure to center of lantern. The difference may be the lantern and the height measure; not resolved. The story states both figures as a disagreement.

The temporary light first shone on May 1, 1871 (LighthouseFriends); the Digital Archive records the station as established in 1871 and the tower as established in 1872. Both are consistent with a temporary light in 1871 and the permanent tower in 1872.

notes_for_editor: The roster is the Digital Archive's (NARA registers via the Kraig Anderson inventory); no individual keeper was confirmed against a primary register here. The 1981 form's acrylic optic (1981) conflicts with the Digital Archive and LighthouseFriends, which describe a third-and-a-half-order Fresnel still in place; a site visit or Coast Guard information would settle it. The tower height (40 ft form; 45 ft LighthouseFriends and Digital Archive) and the record's 13.5 m need a check. The record's range (45 nm) is not supported by any source we read, and the 'order 3' lens conflicts with the sources' third-and-a-half order. The 1931 Bulletin's efficiency-pennant list (keeper Richard F. Dixon for Hospital Point) is garbled in the OCR, so it is not cited. The 1916 Bulletin listing Hospital Point under oil-vapor conversion is garbled and not used. LighthouseFriends' 1909 Taft anecdote and the 1960s rear-admiral anecdote were left out. The 1927 Bulletin article on the spire light is badly garbled in the OCR, so the spire facts rest on the index and LighthouseFriends. Chronicling America returned HTTP 520 for every search tried (none succeeded), so no newspaper material is used. The Palmer Island detail (Small's 1938 hurricane) belongs to Palmer Island, not this station; it is included only as LighthouseFriends' account of his transfer. The 1938 hurricane death is a family detail of a keeper who died long ago; kept to one clause. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the story now states the 40-foot (1981 form) and 45-foot (LighthouseFriends, Digital Archive) tower heights as a disagreement. The Digital Archive is cited for the 1947 automation and roster lines; roster lines were matched by name and position (0.06 km), and the Bulletin efficiency-flag names sit on the same line as Hospital Point in the 1925 and 1926 lists, not by column position. The 'open only at Beverly Homecoming' note and the 2009 Auxiliary openings are both LighthouseFriends statements; the story says the sources do not settle how often it opens now.
